subject: Payment hold: invoice 2026-09 — usage spike, VAT evidence request
messages:
From: Alan Ward <alan.ward@dataloom.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@dataloom.com
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 08:43:00 +0100
Subject: Payment hold — invoice INV-98421 / usage spike & VAT classification

Connor,

We've placed payment for invoice INV-98421 (September 2026) on hold pending clarification. Our finance team saw an unexpected ~1.8M token overage compared to our historical baseline and VAT was charged to our EU entity (we had expected reverse-charge). Before we release payment we need:

- A raw usage export (token-level if possible) for 2026-09-01 -> 2026-09-28; we need request ids and timestamps
- An explanation of whether any backfill/rehydration jobs ran on your platform that could have caused duplicate counting
- Confirmation of how VAT was applied and whether you can reissue net of VAT pending verification (we are an EU-registered VAT payer; VAT ID attached in procurement@dataloom.com)

We understand accounting windows are tight. To avoid wider supplier payment issues we'll hold the invoice until we have evidence. Please respond with an ETA — we need something actionable within 48 hours or we'll escalate to our legal/procurement team.

I've attached the payment hold notice we issued internally.

Thanks,
Alan Ward
CFO, DataLoom Inc.
[Attachment: payment_hold_notice.pdf]
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Alan Ward <alan.ward@dataloom.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 10:15:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Payment hold — invoice INV-98421 / usage spike & VAT classification

Hi Alan — thank you for the heads up and sorry for the noise. We take payment holds seriously and will prioritize a packet of evidence. Quick notes: 

- We're pulling the token-level export and tokenization logs now; I attached an initial billing snapshot while we gather the full export.
- We will check for known causes (embed backfill, duplicate ingest, staging keys routed to production).
- For VAT: if you can re-send the EU VAT ID to procurement@redwood.com we'll engage tax and reissue net of VAT where appropriate; we do need to confirm whether reverse-charge applies.

Provisional offer: to keep your supply chain moving we can apply an interim, reversible credit of up to 50% of the disputed overage (applied as a negative line on your next invoice) while our audit completes. That's not a final admission, but a bridge while we produce token-level evidence. 

Can we schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow to walk the export? I'm available 10:30–12:00 CET. If that works I'll loop in our SRE/Finance.

Connor O'Brien
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: initial_billing_snapshot.csv]
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alan Ward <alan.ward@dataloom.com>, Priya Singh <priya@dataloom.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2026 09:05:00 +0100
Subject: Additional context and preliminary findings — INV-98421 overage

Alan / Priya — adding a little more technical color from the ops side so you have actionable items while the export finishes: 

1) Preliminary trace shows two likely contributors during the 09/10–09/14 window: 
   - A staggered embed re-ingest job (customer-initiated backfill) that replayed older vectors; when combined with our streaming ingest it doubled per-object tokenization for a short period. We have event ids and start/stop timestamps in the export.
   - A mis-tagged staging API key that was inadvertently used against your production tenant for ~18 hours on 2026-09-12; those calls were billed as production. We're correlating API key IDs to your tenant.

2) Next steps I'm running now (ETA EOD 2026-10-02): a deduping pass on the usage window and a prefix attribution audit to separate staging vs production calls. We'll produce a token-level CSV (request_id, timestamp, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens) and a short RCA.

3) Drive link (shared read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-usage-export — full CSV will be uploaded by EOD.

We'll also include a short mapping of which tokens, if any, we propose to credit. If the overage is due to the backfill + staging mis-tag, we'll recommend a retrospective adjustment rather than a full reversal. 

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
S: +1 (415) 555-0199
[Attachment: usage_export_2026-09-01_to_09-28.csv]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alan Ward <alan.ward@dataloom.com>
Cc: Finance Billing <billing@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 14:20:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Payment hold — invoice INV-98421 / usage spike & VAT classification

Alan — thanks for your patience. I'm stepping in to ensure we close this quickly. Summary and immediate actions from Redwood: 

- We will apply a provisional credit of EUR 12,350 (approx. 50% of the disputed overage line) as a negative on your next invoice effective immediately. This is corrective and reversible pending the audit outcome.
- Ben & SRE will deliver the full token-level export and a short RCA by EOD 2026-10-02. If the audit shows over-attribution to production due to our staging key leak, we'll finalize a retrospective adjustment.
- VAT: To reissue net of VAT under the EU reverse-charge, we need your valid VAT ID (please confirm) and we will ask our tax team to reissue an invoice within 5 business days if eligibility is confirmed.

Please confirm receipt of the provisional credit application and share the VAT ID with procurement@redwood.com. If you need the credit applied sooner (cash collection window), flag that now and we'll escalate the finance request.

I've attached a short mutual action plan (MAP) to document the audit steps and timelines — if you can sign and return we can use that to unblock any procurement hold.

Best,
Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success (EMEA), Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MAP_Dataloom_escrow_signed.pdf]
